answer: A cheap stack of new keys cannot claim extra seats at the west orchard bench. Each claimant walks to terrace 7, picks the one apricot tagged for that hour, cracks the pit, and weighs the dry kernel at 19 C (2.10-2.25 g). The clerk fills an 8 ml crystal vial with pit-wash and logs turbidity 4.2-6.0 NTU on the morning card. Cost: one tagged fruit, a 40-minute walk, and a 6 POA fee. Staff re-weigh the kernel and match the vial lot; a hoarded kernel fails because fresh pith turns ivory to brown in 12 minutes. If either check misses, the seat is refused.
